column1: # type-debt-by-type.tsv - OPUS 2026-09-20. The type store measured in BYTES, not in readiness rungs.
# GENERATED by gen_debt.py - the header lives in the generator, so a regeneration does not lose it.
# WHY. "N types at SIGNATURE RESOLVED" is a RUNG COUNT and says nothing about magnitude. It misled me seven
# separate times in one session - S-02 (69,584 bytes asserted unknown against 10,621 measured), S-03 (typed arrays
# called opaque), S-36 (2.8 %), S-41 (named-and-typed rows read as unexplained), S-15 (8.7 %), S-18 (0.7 %) and
# S-49 (a rung count where a byte figure existed). Every time the store was in better shape than the statistic.
# COLUMNS. declared = the type's extent. described = the sum of its field rows. unexplained = bytes in rows whose
# NAME marks them unobserved/padding/gap/reserved/unknown OR whose ctype is a bare `u8[N]` blob with N >= 16,
# PLUS any shortfall where the rows do not reach the declared extent.
# THE TEST WAS WIDENED THE SAME DAY IT WAS PUBLISHED, AND THE FIGURE ROSE FROM 13.2 % TO 22.0 %. The first
# version used the NAME test alone. That understated the debt, because a span can carry a real name and still
# have entirely unknown contents - the 64 KiB `buffer02C8` inside ManagerSub0209AC30_00C0 is the clearest case,
# and the `region0140` / `regionB140` rows added to MapScreenPage an hour later would have scored as explained
# purely for being named. THE NUMBER ROSE BECAUSE THE INSTRUMENT GOT STRICTER, NOT BECAUSE THE STORE GOT WORSE:
# 13.2 % was wrong and 22.0 % is the corrected reading of the same store. The widened test over-counts in the
# other direction - a genuinely understood array such as NavigationPathState's `predecessors u8[128]` is scored
# unexplained for having a bare blob ctype - and that is the safer of the two errors, so it stands.
# WHAT IT MEASURES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Coverage is one of three different questions the store answers; the
# others are type-level readiness and field-row readiness counts. NONE implies the others: a type can be 100 %
# covered and rightly DISCOVERED, and a type can be mostly DISCOVERED by row count and 97 % covered. A low rung
# means "recovered from a sample, not read"; a high unexplained percentage means "nobody knows what these bytes
# are". Only the second is a magnitude.
# A WORKED CASE OF WHY A FIELD MAP AND A DEBT FIGURE ARE DIFFERENT. MapScreenPage was the largest debt row at
# 48,118 of 48,136. A 33-function census of its three page procedures turned one blind 48,102-byte span into
# FIFTY-ONE named fields - and moved the debt by 342 bytes, because the bulk is a single core between +0x13C and
# +0xB1A0 that no censused function touches. Structure improved enormously; magnitude barely moved.
# AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT DID MOVE IT. A census asks "what does this object touch". For a region the object does
# not write but HANDS OUT, the right question is "who is given a pointer into it". Scanning for `lea reg,[page+d]`
# with d inside the core and pairing each with the call that consumes it split that 45,156-byte blind span into
# TWO REGIONS WITH NAMED CONSUMERS: 0xB000 at +0x140 handed to 00402A40 from three sites, and 0x60 at +0xB140
# handed to 00402D20. Contents still unknown, so both still count as debt here - but they are now bounded,
# attributed regions rather than one blind span.
# WHERE THE RESIDUE LIVES, after working the top of this list. It is not diffuse and not one kind of thing:
#   (a) LARGE PRIVATE AREAS the owning object does not write. MapScreenPage's core survived a 33-function census;
#       ActiveLogWidget40C8's 16 KiB survived an 8-function one that found only FOUR fields of its own. These are
#       examined and empty - the handoff scan above is the instrument that works on them, not more census.
#       PApplication 4,400 and the rest of category 22). Extents and names came wholesale from reflection
#       registrations and the interiors were never read. A reading task, not a census task.
#   (c) A LONG TAIL of small gaps inside well-carved types - the source of the percentages in 00, 17 and 19, and
# REGISTERING A TYPE HONESTLY RAISES THIS NUMBER. Several of the top rows are types registered the same day, with
# truthful unobserved spans. Before those rows existed the same bytes were unexplained AND unmeasurable, because
# no type declared them. A RISE after a registration pass is the expected sign; a FALL is the thing to check.
# Rows with an unparseable size cell are skipped.
# THREE BUCKETS, 2026-09-20 (OPUS) - replacing a single figure that conflated two states.
# The old `unexplained` column counted a bare u8[N>=16] the same as a span nobody has looked at.
# Those are not the same thing, and the difference was large enough that the store briefly had to
# quote a BRACKET (9.4 % to 18.2 %) instead of a number. It now measures the split:
#   unobserved            nobody has looked - the NAME says unobserved/padding/gap/reserved/unknown,
#                         plus any declared-minus-described shortfall (bytes with no row at all).
#   identified_uncarved   a bare u8[N>=16] region whose name does NOT say unobserved. We know what
#                         the span IS and not what is inside it.
#   unexplained           kept as the SUM of those two so nothing reading the old column breaks -
#                         but it is a sum of two different things and both are now beside it.
# WHY THE SECOND BUCKET IS NOT DEBT IN THE SAME SENSE. ManagerSub0209AC30_00C0 +0x2C8 is 65,536 of
# it, and that region was established on 2026-09-20 as a FLAT BYTE BUFFER - read `movzx eax, byte
# [rbx]` / `inc rbx` in a copy loop bounded by a global, never strided and never indexed - so there
# is no interior to carve and the row is already the right description. SavePayload's two
# battleStateMirror spans are BattleSystemState's bytes by construction. Chasing those would produce
# nothing; chasing the FIRST bucket produces layout.
# AND A PROCESS NOTE THAT COST A PUBLISHED PARAGRAPH. A note added to the ARTIFACT rather than to
# this header is destroyed by the next regeneration. That is what this file exists to prevent, and
# on 2026-09-20 I wrote the bracket note into the artifact anyway and regenerated over it hours
